title: Ordinary intrinsic pro-étale direct image: K-injective and bounded-below comparison
statement:
Let $f:X	o Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $B$ be a finite commutative ring, including the zero ring. Fix representatives of the small étale and pro-étale sites small in the universe of module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. On each site use intrinsic sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $B_W$ for $W=X,Y$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and their ordinary uncompleted derived categories $D(W_s,B)$, $s\in\{\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet}\}$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the module direct images induced by $f$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image]. Write $
u_W^*$ for the module comparison inverse image [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], with intrinsic constant-section presentation [lem-pe-coefficient-comparison-data]. Then both module direct images have total right derived functors $Rf_{s,*}$ on the full ordinary derived categories in the sense of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. For every K-injective resolution $M	o I$ their values are canonically $Rf_{s,*}M\cong Q(f_{s,*}I)$, where $Q$ is derived localization. On bounded-below objects these functors identify naturally with the usual bounded-below right derived direct images $Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}:D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)	o D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ and $Rf_{\mathrm{proet},*}:D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)	o D^+(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]; a bounded-below complex of injectives computes both constructions, and the identifications respect their derived-functor units. The intrinsic constant-section module inverse image and the module inverse image $
u_W^*$ are canonically isomorphic as left adjoints to the same sectionwise module direct image $
u_{W,*}$. Under these identifications, for every $G\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ there is a natural isomorphism in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$
$$
u_Y^*Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}G\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{\mathrm{proet},*}
u_X^*G,$$
which is the bounded-below direct-image comparison isomorphism of [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] (for $u=f$, $\Lambda=B$, $L=G$) after inclusion into the full derived category. Here $D^+$ means vanishing cohomology in all sufficiently negative degrees [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], and the derived $
u_W^*$ is termwise inverse image followed by localization [lem-pe-coefficient-comparison-derived-functor]. No claim is made for étale inputs with unbounded-below cohomology.

proof.text: For each $W=X,Y$ and $s=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet}$, put $\mathcal A_{W,s}=\operatorname{Mod}(B_W)$. The chosen site is small in the coefficient universe and $B_W$ is a sheaf of commutative rings. Apply [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] to this ringed site: $\mathcal A_{W,s}$ is Grothendieck abelian and every complex has a K-injective resolution. By [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] it also has enough ordinary injectives. These statements apply to the intrinsic module category, without replacing it by a category of externally valued sheaves.

source.place: Tag 07A5, section-unbounded, opening paragraph; injectives.tex Tags 079H and 079P

proof.text: Write $F_s=f_{s,*}$. Its section formula and ring action are [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] for the etale site and [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] for the pro-etale site. Addition of maps is componentwise, so $F_s$ is additive. Kernels and finite products of module sheaves are sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; evaluating them at $V\times_Y X$ and restricting scalars along $B_Y(V)\to B_X(V\times_Y X)$ preserves those kernels and products. Thus $F_s$ is left exact on both intrinsic module categories.

source.place: Tag 071J, section-derived-functors, module direct image; sites-modules.tex Tag 03D6, definition-pushforward

proof.text: Apply $F_s$ degreewise. Additivity preserves the equations defining chain homotopies, shifts, and the differential of a mapping cone: $F_s(C\oplus A[1])=F_s(C)\oplus F_s(A)[1]$, with the same differential matrix. Hence it induces an exact functor $K(\mathcal A_{X,s})\to K(\mathcal A_{Y,s})$, and composition with derived localization gives an exact functor to $D(\mathcal A_{Y,s})$. The K-injective existence proved in step 1 is precisely the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. Applying it gives the total right derived functor $RF_s$ with its unit, in the sense of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Its unit at a K-injective $I$ is invertible. For a resolution $C\to I$, applying $RF_s$ to $QC\cong QI$ therefore gives $RF_s(QC)\cong Q(F_s I)$, as asserted.

By [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], every object $M\in D^+(\mathcal A_{X,s})$ is $QJ$ up to isomorphism for a bounded-below complex of injectives $J$, and $J$ is K-injective. Step 3 then computes $RF_sM$ by $Q(F_sJ)$. Since $F_s(0)=0$, this complex is bounded below, so $RF_s$ restricts to $D^+$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] to the additive $F_s$ and the enough-injectives category of step 1. It gives the usual bounded-below functor $R^+F_s$, whose unit at $J$ is invertible and whose value at $Q^+J$ is $Q^+(F_sJ)$. Thus both constructions are computed on the same $J$. This is the bounded-below etale direct image of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]; for the ordinary pro-etale operation of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] it specifies its bounded-below restriction.

source.place: Tag 013K, lemma-injective-resolutions-exist; Tag 070J, lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective; Tags 05TI, lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived, and 05TH, lemma-injective-acyclic; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 071J

proof.text:
The identifications in step 4 are natural and normalized by the units. For a morphism represented by bounded-below injective complexes $J,J'$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] gives a unique homotopy class $h:J\to J'$ representing it. Naturality of the invertible units [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived, lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] identifies both images with $Q(F_sh)$. Changing the injective models uses a homotopy equivalence, whose image under the additive $F_s$ is again a homotopy equivalence. At $QJ$ define $\theta_{QJ}=\alpha_J\eta_J^{-1}$, where $\eta,\alpha$ are the full and bounded-below units and inclusions into the full categories are understood. The preceding naturality makes these components independent of models and natural on $D^+$. For a bounded-below complex $C$, [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution-existence] supplies a quasi-isomorphism $s:C\to J$ with bounded-below injective target. Explicitly,
$$\theta_{QC}=R^+F_s(Q^+s)^{-1}\alpha_J\eta_J^{-1}RF_s(Qs).$$
Naturality of the two units gives $RF_s(Qs)\eta_C=\eta_JQ(F_ss)$ and $R^+F_s(Q^+s)\alpha_C=\alpha_JQ(F_ss)$. Substitution into the formula yields $\theta_{QC}\eta_C=\alpha_C$. This proves compatibility with the derived-functor units.

source.place: Tags 070I, lemma-K-injective, and 070K, lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies; Tag 013K, lemma-injective-resolutions-exist

proof.text: For $W=X,Y$, [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] gives the geometric morphism $\nu_W$ and the sectionwise right adjoint: $(\nu_{W,*}N)(U)=N(u_WU)$. Its fixed-$B$ action and its intrinsic constant-ring module action agree: for a constant scalar $b$ both act by the same endomorphism $b:N(u_WU)\to N(u_WU)$; the ring map from $B_W$ is determined by these constant sections by sheafification. The intrinsic constant-section presentation in [lem-pe-coefficient-comparison-data] uses this ring map. The constant-ring inverse-image construction and its exactness are [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image], and [lem-weil-pbc-module-inverse-image-unit-comparison] supplies its normalized module-pullback unit. Both inverse-image presentations are therefore left adjoint to this same module right adjoint. Explicitly, if $L\dashv R$ and $L\prime\dashv R$ are these presentations, define $a_M:LM\to L\prime M$ to be the adjunct of $\eta\prime_M:M\to RL\prime M$ under the first adjunction; define $b_M$ in the reverse way from $\eta_M$. The adjunction bijections give $R(a_M)\eta_M=\eta\prime_M$ and $R(b_M)\eta\prime_M=\eta_M$, so $b_Ma_M$ and $a_Mb_M$ correspond to the respective units and are identities. The adjunct formulas also prove naturality. This is the canonical, unit-preserving isomorphism of inverse images required in the statement.

The exact intrinsic $
u_W^*$ descends termwise through localization and commutes with cohomology by [lem-pe-coefficient-comparison-derived-functor]. Thus it preserves $D^+$, and the natural isomorphism of step 6 descends termwise as well. Since $f$ is qcqs and $G\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)$, [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image], with $u=f$, $\Lambda=B$, and $L=G$, supplies $c_G:
u_Y^*R^+F_{\mathrm{et}}G\xrightarrow{\sim}R^+F_{\mathrm{proet}}
u_X^*G$. Let $	heta_s:RF_s|_{D^+}\xrightarrow{\sim}R^+F_s$ denote the identification of steps 4-5, with inclusions into the full categories understood. The required arrow is exactly the composite $	heta_{\mathrm{proet},
u_X^*G}^{-1}\circ c_G\circ
u_Y^*(	heta_{\mathrm{et},G})$, using the inverse-image identification of step 6. Each factor is natural and invertible, so the composite is a natural isomorphism. This formula also proves that it is the specified bounded-below comparison after inclusion, with its direct-image units unchanged by step 5. Only bounded-below inputs were used; no extension to unbounded-below etale inputs follows.
